findings.title: OUTPUT_PENDING callback rules conflict
anchors: While OUTPUT_PENDING, no inbound message or callback may dispatch, publish readiness or reenter the owner.
A completion delivered synchronously is queued like an asynchronous completion.
findings.observation: The first rule prohibits every callback from reentering the owner while the later algorithm requires the active send completion to be serialized and published through that owner.
findings.required_resolution: Exclude only the active output completion from the general callback prohibition, define how it is queued and serialized, and state that unrelated callbacks retain no admission or publication authority.

findings.title: Protected call concurrency is unspecified
anchors: At most one control request is outstanding.
One owner exclusively controls one role, authenticated peer/key tuple, SAGE session, connection incarnation, pending invocation, MCP phase and request-ID history.
findings.observation: The draft limits control requests and models a singular pending invocation, but it does not say whether READY permits one or several outstanding protected calls or how multiple responses interact with OUTPUT_PENDING and closure.
findings.required_resolution: Choose a protected-call concurrency limit and define reservation, response correlation, publication ordering, backpressure, deadline and close behavior for attempts at or beyond that limit.

findings.title: The local binding and descriptor baseline lack a stable selection identifier
anchors: Both hosts MUST select this binding through trusted deployment configuration, before parsing traffic.
There is no unprotected probe, fallback, new cipher, transcript field or portable authorization token.
Expanding this binding requires an explicit profile/descriptor revision and verifier and interoperability evidence before advertisement.
findings.observation: Preconfiguration can avoid wire negotiation, but the draft does not assign a stable binding identifier or normative descriptor digest that both deployments can compare before opening a session.
findings.required_resolution: Define a versioned local profile identifier and pin the complete descriptor digest in the adopted profile or registry. Construction must fail before setup when configured identifiers or descriptor digests differ.

findings.title: The proposal has not been reconciled with the normative baseline
anchors: Before adoption: independently review this state machine and fixed acknowledgement;
update the normative profile, traceability and compatibility/change record together;
findings.observation: The consolidated document is still a proposal layered over an unpublished baseline, so its MUST statements do not yet have one normative owner or compatibility status.
findings.required_resolution: Apply the accepted text atomically to the normative profile, traceability, compatibility record and changelog, with one reviewable revision and no competing rule source.

findings.title: Current execution evidence is not linked from the adoption record
anchors: Earlier 40/58-case reports remain historical, not total coverage of this integrated draft.
findings.observation: The historical plans correctly remain NOT_RUN, while Inspector now derives current 71-case evidence. An adoption reader has no pinned normative link that distinguishes and locates those two states.
findings.required_resolution: Keep the historical plan immutable and add an adoption evidence record that pins the Inspector revision, contracts, CI artifacts and derived current results without rewriting plan status.

findings.title: External independent review is still required
findings.observation: This internal rereview can identify and freeze issues but cannot satisfy the proposal requirement for scrutiny by an independent external reviewer.
findings.required_resolution: After ADOPT-01 through ADOPT-05 are resolved in one candidate, obtain an external review of the state machine, fixed acknowledgement, final admission ordering, deadlines, algorithm boundary and excluded transports.
